author: NorthEast News Desk
body: Former Fall River Mayor Jasiel Correia has agreed to pay $170 a month toward more than $306,000 in outstanding restitution after completing his federal prison sentence in July. The payment schedule appears in federal court documents filed this week and can be reviewed as his financial circumstances change.

Correia was convicted in 2021 on public-corruption charges and received a six-year prison sentence. He had been ordered to pay more than $310,000 in restitution. The new plan reflects his current employment and reported finances rather than reducing the amount owed. Federal probation officials can periodically reassess his ability to pay and seek adjustments to the monthly figure.

Court filings identify Correia’s current job as a full-time marketing manager at the Towne House. Restitution plans are intended to keep repayment active after incarceration while allowing supervision officials to account for a defendant’s income and expenses. The case remains a prominent chapter in Fall River politics because the criminal conduct occurred while Correia held office. The latest filing sets the immediate repayment terms but leaves open the possibility of higher installments if his financial position improves.
dek: Federal filings show Jasiel Correia still owes more than $306,000, with the payment amount subject to periodic review.
headline: Former Fall River mayor begins $170 monthly restitution plan
